bug_semantics: Attacker-controlled template expressions were evaluated as Python with a live rendering context. In the 0.1.x interpolation path, `{{ x.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}` passed a context-rooted dotted expression to raw `eval`; an empty globals dictionary is not a sandbox, because Python attribute traversal from any ordinary context object reaches the process object graph and can recover classes, module globals, and command-execution primitives. The 0.2.0-alpha rewrite retained the defect: `ExpressionEvaluator` either walked arbitrary attributes/methods or routed expressions containing an operator to `safe_eval`, which called raw `eval` with only `__builtins__` emptied. Commit 62c95c472fbd9ca5630a989ddec9d8899256726a replaced those paths with an AST interpreter that rejects underscore-prefixed attributes and restricts callable methods/builtins.
flaw_origin: The smallest real BIC for the reported `{{ ... }}` SSTI path is 2afc2aa5c29a413db5bf26fb0ef39fc6a18fec78 (`Add the possibility to call variables methods in the template`). It widened both interpolation regexes from simple `\w+` names to arbitrary expressions and added `variable_value = eval(".".join(expression), {}, context)` in `pyblade/engine/parser.py`. Its immediate parent only looked up a simple captured name and could not send dotted interpolation syntax to Python evaluation. The later c539c2a5c3bfb0e07d41b35a0e4b1cf3fb51b89a split/moved this same sink to `pyblade/engine/parsing/variables.py`, and 806f68cdab59694b780f3af0f0a6f7a535bbd08d replaced it with another unsafe evaluator for 0.2.0-alpha; neither later commit is the origin. The issue's separate assertion that `_is_safe_ast` in 0.1.8-alpha accepts a Constant-rooted `''.__class__` payload is contradicted by that tag's tree and by execution: the Attribute branch returns false unless the base is an allowed Name/attribute pair, and the sandbox is not called by the tagged rendering path. The real 0.1.x sink is the context-rooted interpolation eval above.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object (`git cat-file -p 2afc2aa5c29a413db5bf26fb0ef39fc6a18fec78`) records human author and committer `AntaresMugisho <antaresmugisho@gmail.com>` and only the message `Add the possibility to call variables methods in the template`; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/AntaresMugisho/PyBlade/issues/1 describes SSTI/RCE for 0.1.8-alpha through 0.2.0-alpha and identifies 62c95c47 as the main-branch fix; the maintainer confirmed that fix in the issue on 2026-04-08 and said it was not yet released.

`git diff 04922ab0ea7f509c9c6cbcc1eca1fbab60d6fd1d 2afc2aa5c29a413db5bf26fb0ef39fc6a18fec78 -- pyblade/engine/parser.py` shows the BIC widening `{{ }}` and `{!! !!}` matching from `\w+` to arbitrary content, splitting the captured expression on dots, and adding raw `eval(".".join(expression), {}, context)`. The parent version performs only `context[var_name]`; the vulnerable interpolation mechanism is absent from the immediate parent tree.

`git log -L` follows the sink from 2afc2aa5c29a413db5bf26fb0ef39fc6a18fec78 through non-causal edits and then to c539c2a5c3bfb0e07d41b35a0e4b1cf3fb51b89a, whose subject says it split the parser into modules and whose new `pyblade/engine/parsing/variables.py` preserves the same eval. Thus c539c2a5c3bfb0e07d41b35a0e4b1cf3fb51b89a is a move/refactor, not the BIC.

A scoped execution of the exact sink semantics, `eval("x.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()", {}, {"x": ""})`, returned a Python list of 215 subclasses, confirming that an ordinary context object escapes the purported empty-globals sandbox into the object graph.

`git grep` on release trees finds the inherited sink at `v0.1.4-alpha:pyblade/engine/parser.py:79` and `v0.1.8-alpha:pyblade/engine/parsing/variables.py:93`; therefore the BIC predates the advisory's affected lower boundary and the repository indicates that the vulnerable interpolation behavior was already present in v0.1.4-alpha. `git tag --contains 2afc...` lists v0.1.4-alpha, v0.1.8-alpha, v.0.1.9-alpha, and v0.2.0-alpha.

For the 0.2.0-alpha lifecycle leg, `git log -L` identifies 806f68cdab59694b780f3af0f0a6f7a535bbd08d as creation of `pyblade/engine/evaluator.py`; the v0.2.0-alpha tree contains `return eval(expression, {"__builtins__": builtins}, context)` at line 36. Merge-base checks place 806f... after tag v.0.1.9-alpha (28bc24a9977504061248377d3d241d0d9b366dcc) and as an ancestor of v0.2.0-alpha (559b9edd61c18723011a0f4509aa66fb44999c24). This is a continuation/reimplementation of the already-existing template-evaluation flaw, not its first origin.

The report's proposed 0.1.8-alpha Constant-rooted AST bypass was checked directly against `v0.1.8-alpha:pyblade/engine/sandbox.py`: `_is_safe_ast(ast.parse("''.__class__", mode="eval"))` returned false and `safe_eval` raised `SafeEvalException: ... Unsafe expression detected`. `git grep safe_eval v0.1.8-alpha -- pyblade` finds definitions only in sandbox.py and no renderer caller. This is why the BIC is based on the reachable raw-eval interpolation sink rather than the report's non-reproducing sandbox explanation.

`git show 62c95c472fbd9ca5630a989ddec9d8899256726a -- pyblade/engine` deletes `pyblade/engine/evaluator.py` and adds `pyblade/engine/sandbox.py` with `SafeEvaluator`, AST-node interpretation, restricted builtins/operators, and an Attribute guard rejecting names beginning `_`; this directly cuts the object-model chain and removes raw eval from the rendering evaluator. The issue independently names the same commit as the fix, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are identical.

Release-boundary checks show `git tag --contains 62c95c472fbd9ca5630a989ddec9d8899256726a` returns no tag, while v0.2.0-alpha's merge base with the fix is the tag commit 559b9edd61c18723011a0f4509aa66fb44999c24. This agrees with the advisory's null first_patched_version and the maintainer's statement that users must consume main for the fix.

The BIC commit object has tree 2aafa572c0dc4813d6e424a6f4c8c3812458dd30, parent 04922ab0ea7f509c9c6cbcc1eca1fbab60d6fd1d, author/committer AntaresMugisho <antaresmugisho@gmail.com>, and no trailers or bot/AI marker. AI attribution was evaluated only on this BIC object.
reasoning: The advisory's stated AST-validation story does not survive source and behavioral checking for 0.1.8-alpha: the cited Constant attribute is rejected, and that sandbox has no rendering caller. The repository nevertheless proves a real, remotely relevant template-code-execution primitive in the affected lifecycle. Commit 2afc2aa5c29a413db5bf26fb0ef39fc6a18fec78 is the first commit that lets arbitrary dotted `{{ ... }}` expressions reach Python eval; a context-rooted payload traverses `__class__`, `__mro__`, and `__subclasses__` despite empty globals. Direct comparison with parent 04922ab0ea7f509c9c6cbcc1eca1fbab60d6fd1d proves that interpolation path absent there. The sink survives a module split in c539c2a5c3bfb0e07d41b35a0e4b1cf3fb51b89a and is reimplemented unsafely in 806f68cdab59694b780f3af0f0a6f7a535bbd08d for v0.2.0-alpha. Tag checks place the BIC before every advisory-listed affected release (and reveal the same sink in v0.1.4-alpha), while the direct fix 62c95c472fbd9ca5630a989ddec9d8899256726a lands after v0.2.0-alpha and is not in any release tag. That fix removes the raw evaluator and blocks private attribute traversal in an AST interpreter. Because the smallest real BIC's commit object is a normal human AntaresMugisho commit with no AI/bot identity or AI/co-author/generated trailer, the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI. The causal/AI judgment is closed; only distribution of the already-committed fix remains open.
remaining_gap: The security fix exists on main at 62c95c472fbd9ca5630a989ddec9d8899256726a, but no release tag contains it and the advisory still has no first_patched_version. The maintainer's 2026-04-08 issue comment explicitly says the fix is not yet released, so users of published packages remain without a patched release boundary.
